title: Event-driven GUIs with Tkinter

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
Tkinter builds desktop tools from windows and controls; callbacks should return quickly so the event loop can respond.
CORE EXPLANATION

Tkinter is Python's standard-library interface for desktop graphical applications. Widgets such as Label, Entry, and Button are arranged with geometry managers; callbacks handle clicks and keyboard events, while mainloop waits for window events. Unlike a terminal script, the application remains active until the window closes.
EXAMPLE CODE
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
import tkinter as tk

root = tk.Tk()
message = tk.StringVar(value='Hazır')
label = tk.Label(root, textvariable=message)
label.pack(padx=12, pady=8)
tk.Button(root, text='Salam', command=lambda: message.set('Salam!')).pack()
root.mainloop()

spans.text: EXPECTED RESULT

spans.code: A window opens with a button; clicking it changes the label to Salam!.

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Keep callbacks short: long work can block the event loop and freeze the window.

spans.title: Warning
spans.text: Never execute user-entered text with eval/exec; GUI input is untrusted.
